name: Farmers market / open-air pavilion
summary: Open-sided roofed pavilion (steel or heavy timber) over vendor stalls/drive aisles with lighting, power at columns, water, and usually a restroom building. Public bids give ≈ $57/SF of roof for a structure-only canopy (2015) and ≈ $540k for a ~20-stall street pavilion (2022, restrooms extra). The default includes a pro-rata restroom and site/utility allowance, so it sits above structure-only bids.

typicalSize.method: e1 15,000 SF roof; e2 ~20 vehicle stalls (≈ 6,000–9,000 SF). Mid 10,000 SF of covered area.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Covered SF per acre of market site including aisles, parking and plaza; pavilions over existing parking lots (e1, e5) are denser. Derived.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Spaces per covered SF; many pavilions sit on lots used as parking on non-market days (e1). Derived.

perPrimaryUnit.method: 2024 dollars per SF of covered area. Structure-only: e1 $56.6/SF (2015) ≈ $80 in 2024; shade/seating pavilion $41/SF (food-truck-park e6, 2022, lighter shade structure). e2 $540k for ~20 stalls (~7,500 SF assumed) ≈ $72/SF (2022) with lighting and power. Default adds restrooms (e3 $150k allowance ÷ 10,000 SF ≈ $15/SF) and site/utility/paving allowance (~$10–15/SF) → mid ≈ $95/SF. Low $50 = basic pre-engineered canopy over existing pavement, no restrooms; high $200 = heavy-timber/architectural pavilion with partially enclosed/heated bays (e4 Rochester-type market halls cost more).

scope.notes: Pavilion structure, slab/pavement under roof, lighting and power at columns, water hose bibs, pro-rata restroom building and on-site utilities. Excludes land, soft costs, vendor fixtures, off-sites, impact/tap fees.

qualityTiers.method: economy ≈ low/mid (50/95); luxury ≈ high/mid (200/95 = 2.1); premium interpolated.

systemSplit.method: Derived: steel/timber frame and roof dominate (05 + 06 + 07 ≈ 38%); footings and slab 03; electrical (lights/power on each pole per e2) ≈ 10%; restroom plumbing 22; paving/landscape 32. Not taken from a published bid breakdown.

lineItems.name: Open-sided pavilion structure and roof (steel or timber, incl. footings)

cost.method: e1 ≈ $57/SF roof structure (2015) and e6 $41/SF shade (2022); heavy timber/architectural roofs at the high end.
e3 $150k allowance (2022); park restroom contracts $265k–$608k (amenities block).

lineItems.name: Vendor power pedestals/receptacles and water stations (per stall)

cost.method: Derived per-stall allowance (e2 includes lights and electricity on each pole). Qty ≈ 1 stall per 250 SF covered.

lineItems.name: Enclosed/heated market bays or winter shed (per SF enclosed)

cost.method: Derived; e4 shows enclosed sheds substantially raise cost. Qty defaults to 0.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Picnic tables, signage, trash receptacles, banners. Derived.

pctOfHard.method: Simple structure: A&E, structural, civil, permits, survey/testing. Public projects add grant administration. Derived.

softCosts.notes: Grant-funded projects often require prevailing wage and Buy-America compliance (soft/admin cost).

design.method: Small public pavilions frequently bid over budget (e2 bid 12% over the $483k budget).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Structure-only canopy (e1 escalated, little soft) to architectural pavilion with restrooms (high × 1.25).

evidence.quote: awarded an $849,000 contract to Maccabee Industrial Inc. ... The 15,000-square-foot roof structure will be constructed as originally designed, and the restrooms and office will be included in another phase
evidence.scopeNotes: Canopy pavilion over existing city parking lots; restrooms/office deferred. $849,000 / 15,000 SF ≈ $56.6/SF of roof (my division). Washington PA is in the Pittsburgh metro.

source.title: Council awards bid for farmers market pavilion

evidence.quote: the $540,215.55 bid, which came in much higher than the project’s $483,000 budget ... stalls providing room for close to 20 vehicles ... The structure will include lights and electricity on each supporting pole.
evidence.scopeNotes: Open-air street-spanning pavilion, ~20 vendor vehicle stalls (≈ $27k per stall); city separately allotted $150,000 for outdoor restrooms. Published 2022-11-24.

source.title: Council awards bid for farmers market pavilion

evidence.quote: Outdoor restrooms have become part of the project as well, for which Obren says the city allotted $150,000.
evidence.scopeNotes: Budget allowance, not a bid; plumbing had to be extended.

evidence.quote: Between 2015 and 2017, the market underwent an $8.3 million renovation ... replaced the 1978 "Wintershed" with a new 13,000-square-foot ... indoor Shed B, constructed a new outdoor Shed D ... added 46 vendor stalls, and installed four food kiosks
evidence.scopeNotes: Mixed scope (enclosed heated shed + open shed + site); upper-bound reference for market buildings, not a simple pavilion.

source.title: Traverse City Commission to vote on $3.67 million Lot B and Farmers Market Pavilion project

evidence.quote: consider awarding a $3.67 million contract Monday to reconstruct Parking Lot B downtown and build the long-planned Farmers Market Pavilion. Elmer’s Crane and Dozer of Traverse City submitted the low bid at $3,334,714.24
evidence.scopeNotes: Combined parking-lot reconstruction + pavilion contract (pavilion share not separated in the article; ~$2.95M funded by TIF). Pavilion area not stated. Context only.
